items.text: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI models, filed publicly Monday to sell shares on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT."
items.detail: The S-1 filed with the SEC does not yet set a share count or price range; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead banks. The filing shows revenue of $16.29 billion for the first half of 2026, up from $1.16 billion a year earlier, and a net loss of $80.7 billion, most of it a $72.4 billion non-cash charge on the value of convertible notes. Anthropic filed confidentially in June; AFP reported it plans to sell shares in mid-November, and AP said the offering could top SpaceX's record $86 billion IPO in June. Separately, Meta on Monday launched a $35 billion stock sale to fund AI spending ($22.5 billion of common stock through forward sales and $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred shares) and plans up to about $60 billion more later.
items.why: One of the leading AI companies is preparing what could be the largest stock market debut ever, as tech giants raise record sums to pay for AI.

items.text: Brazil's main stock index plunged nearly 14% Monday, the first trading day after President Lula's reelection, while U.S. stocks rose.
items.detail: Trading on Brazil's B3 exchange was halted for 30 minutes at the open after the Ibovespa's drop triggered a circuit breaker, and the real fell more than 10% against the dollar, AFP reported. Lula beat Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday's runoff. In New York, the S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,676.77, the Dow added 146.42 points, or 0.3%, to 52,361.58, and the Nasdaq gained 0.8%, led by AI stocks after Anthropic's IPO filing. Verizon reported 406,000 new postpaid phone subscribers in the third quarter, its best third quarter in five years, and raised its 2026 forecast.
items.why: A market crash in Latin America's largest economy hits investors and companies with exposure to Brazil.

items.text: Egypt's parliament authorized military support to help defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks Monday, as talks in Tehran ended with only a pledge to keep talking.
items.detail: The authorization is limited to defending Saudi Arabia and applies only if Riyadh requests help, AP reported. Talks in Tehran between Iranian leaders and delegations from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey ended with an agreement to keep talking and no concrete deal announced. Yemen's Houthis said they attacked pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and Riyadh's airport; Saudi Arabia did not confirm the claims.
items.why: The Houthi war on Saudi Arabia is drawing in more countries as the U.S. weighs new strikes on Iran.

items.text: Forty-eight noncitizens in five states face federal charges of illegal voting or falsely claiming citizenship to register, the Justice Department announced Monday.
items.detail: The cases are in Pennsylvania, California, Florida, New York and Nevada. Most defendants are lawful permanent residents, according to the Justice Department. They are accused of voting in the 2022 or 2024 federal elections, or in one case a June 2026 primary, and some are also charged with lying about their voting or citizenship claims on naturalization applications. The announcement comes eight days before the Nov. 3 midterms. Charges are accusations; the defendants are presumed innocent.
items.why: The administration is pressing its case on noncitizen voting days before the midterms, as courts weigh related voter-roll fights.

items.text: Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts Monday to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as it pours money into AI data centers.
items.detail: Microsoft announced the Voluntary Exit Offer for employees at level 70 and below on participating teams in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and India. About 60,000 of Microsoft's 223,000 workers are eligible, the company confirmed to GeekWire. Employees decide in early December, and those who accept leave Dec. 31, CNBC reported. Some sales, marketing and engineering teams are not taking part. It follows a voluntary retirement program in April and 4,800 layoffs announced in July. Microsoft reports quarterly results Wednesday.
items.why: One of the largest U.S. employers is shrinking its staff by choice as AI reshapes tech jobs.

items.text: Maurene Comey's firing as a federal prosecutor was illegal, a federal judge ruled Monday, ordering the Justice Department to reinstate her.
items.detail: U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman in Manhattan found the July 2025 firing of Comey, a daughter of former FBI Director James Comey, violated the Civil Service Reform Act, the separation of powers, federal administrative law and her due-process rights. He ordered retroactive reinstatement with back pay from July 16, 2025, through Dec. 20, 2025, when she started a new job. Comey had worked on the Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell prosecutions. The Justice Department said it "disagrees with this decision and will appeal in due course." The judge has not yet ruled on her First Amendment claim and ordered further briefing.
items.why: The ruling limits the administration's power to fire career prosecutors without cause.
items.court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York

items.text: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra Monday, a cheaper model built for computer-use and office tasks, priced at half its predecessor's rate.
items.detail: The model is rolling out to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users and to developers through the API at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI said it is the first model in its line rated at the "Critical" cybersecurity threshold under its Preparedness Framework and published added safeguards.
items.why: Cheaper AI agents that can operate computers are moving into everyday office software.

also.text: Kenya released its first 20 Ebola contacts from quarantine Monday after 21 days without symptoms, with case counts holding at nine.
also.detail: Health ministry Director-General Patrick Amoth said the seven surviving patients are stable and 98 people still in quarantine will be released in four waves starting Nov. 3. Two patients have died. All cases of the Bundibugyo strain are tied to one cluster linked to the index patient, who died Oct. 5, Reuters reported.
also.why: The outbreak appears contained to one cluster so far.
